description: An external busy period after this node's own transmission delays the idle, so the held timer takes lbt_wait_dcd_ms rather than K-0074's VDCD value, but it is not a busy period for K-0086: the last transmission is still this node's, and slotted contention keeps the extra slot of K-0082. The input only ever makes the node more cautious.
note: The set-up to 35550 is that of csma-slotted-own-last-tx: two S_UNIDATA_REQUESTs (priority 0 to SAP 5 at 0.0.1.3, U_PDU "hello", no confirmation, A-0095, K-0096), the first sent at the LBT expiry at 30000 (position 1, zero contention), the second arriving in LINKING and waiting for the next transmission (K-0095). Both transmissions are one block of 5550 ms on wn 2 long, each a single-segment NON-ARQ-DATA D_PDU with C_PDU IDs 0 and 1 (C-0326, C-1040) and the EOT and reception window of that scenario. At 35550 the transmission ends: LBT_WAIT with lbt_wait_vdcd_ms, 3000 ms (K-0074). channel_busy true at 36000 holds csma.lbt_wait (K-0006, K-0077, K-0087). The external input clears at 37000, after our transmission ended and with no EOT prediction in force, so it delayed the idle: a DCD-determined idle, so 30000 ms (K-0006, K-0120, K-0070). The input is not a busy period for K-0086 (K-0006), so the last transmission is still ours and the expiry at 67000 computes CONT_WAIT_TIMER_VALUE as 1 x 3000 ms (K-0082), as csma-slotted-own-last-tx does; counting it would give (1 - 1) x 3000 = 0 ms and let the input shorten the wait. At 70000 the node enters LINKING and sends the second C_PDU (K-0090). The transmitted bytes equal that scenario's second transmission, since its D_PDU fields do not depend on when it is sent.
